claims.text: Superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys is governed by the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Chemical disorder modulates the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Atomic size mismatch modulates the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The initial HEA has a random atomic distribution.
Substitution with elements of differing atomic radii and electronegativities can systematically vary atomic size mismatch and chemical disorder.
The proposed comparison is conducted below the superconducting transition temperature while pressure and magnetic field are controlled.
Chemical disorder affects the electronic band structure.
Atomic size mismatch affects the electronic band structure.
Changes in electronic band structure alter the density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level influences electron-phonon coupling strength.
Electron-phonon coupling strength influences the superconducting transition temperature.
Increasing atomic size mismatch will reduce the density of states at the Fermi level.
Increasing chemical disorder will reduce the density of states at the Fermi level.
A reduced density of states at the Fermi level will lead to a lower superconducting transition temperature.
Reducing atomic size mismatch and chemical disorder will increase the superconducting transition temperature.
An HEA with minimal atomic size mismatch and chemical disorder can serve as the baseline for transition-temperature measurements.
The proposed mechanism applies to metallic-bonded HEAs.
The proposed mechanism does not extend to HEAs dominated by covalent or ionic bonding.
